# origin iam and sts commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v3.2.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin iam` command, and the `origin sts` command that assumes a service account with an identity provider's token. Logging in is `origin id login`; see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md).

## origin iam

Identity and access management: role bindings, service accounts, roles, permissions, your user and the audit log. Role bindings, service accounts and the audit log are an organization's (`--organization`); roles, permissions and your user are the same in every organization. A role binding's member is a full name: a user's `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, which `origin iam lookup-user` finds from a verified email address, or a service account's `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. `origin iam list-role-bindings --organization -` lists the bindings you hold, in every organization.

Every `origin iam` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://iam.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_IAM_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-audit-log-entry

Returns an audit log entry. Needs `iam.audit_log.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-audit-log-entry [OPTIONS] --audit-log-entry <AUDIT_LOG_ENTRY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--audit-log-entry` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--audit-log-entry <AUDIT_LOG_ENTRY>` | yes | The entry to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/auditLogEntries/{audit_log_entry}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/auditLogEntries/{audit_log_entry}`. |

### list-audit-log-entries

Lists an organization's audit log entries, most recent first, optionally only a project's, an actor's or an action's. Needs `iam.audit_log.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-audit-log-entries [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--project <NAME>` | no | Only the entries of changes limited to this project, by its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`. Every entry when empty. Its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--actor <ACTOR>` | no | Only the entries of changes made by this member, by its full name, as a role binding's `member` names it. Every actor's when empty. |
| `--action <ACTION>` | no | Only the entries of this action, such as `iam.role.assign`. Every action's when empty. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most entries to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### get-federated-credential

Returns a federated credential, deleted or not. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` or `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>` | yes | The federated credential to return. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`. |

### list-federated-credentials

Lists a service account's federated credentials, oldest first. Deleted ones are listed only when `--show-deleted` is set. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-federated-credentials [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most federated credentials to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--show-deleted <true|false>` | no | Whether deleted federated credentials are listed too. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |

### create-federated-credential

Creates a federated credential on an active `WORKLOAD` service account. Anyone whose token matches it acts as the service account, so creating one needs `iam.service_account.create` and `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization: the right to act as the account yourself. Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` when a condition contains `*`, or when no condition names an identity that never changes: `repository_id` or `repository_owner_id` for GitHub Actions' issuer, `project_id` or `namespace_id` for GitLab.com's, `terraform_organization_id` for HCP Terraform's, `sub` for any other. A `terraform_run_phase` condition on HCP Terraform's issuer must be `plan` or `apply`.

```sh
origin iam create-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME> --issuer <ISSUER> --condition <KEY=VALUE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | A name of your own, shown in the console; at most 100 characters. |
| `--issuer <ISSUER>` | yes | The identity provider whose tokens are trusted: a token's `iss`, matched exactly, an `https` URL that serves `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, such as `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. |
| `--audience <AUDIENCE>` | no | The audience a token must be issued for, its `aud`, matched exactly; `https://sts.origincloudapis.eu` when the create leaves it empty. |
| `--condition <KEY=VALUE>` | yes | The claims a token must carry, each with exactly this value, such as `repository_id` and `environment` for GitHub Actions. At least one, on an identity that never changes. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day returns the federated credential the first request created, as it is now, instead of creating a second. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT`. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-federated-credential

Deletes a federated credential: no token is exchanged for it from then on, and an access token already exchanged for it is refused on its next request. It stays readable as `DELETED`. Deleting a deleted one succeeds. Needs `iam.service_account.revoke` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam delete-federated-credential [OPTIONS] --federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` or `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Needed unless `--federated-credential` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--federated-credential <FEDERATED_CREDENTIAL>` | yes | The federated credential to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/federatedCredentials/{federated_credential}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-permission

Returns a permission.

```sh
origin iam get-permission [OPTIONS] --permission <PERMISSION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--permission <PERMISSION>` | yes | The permission to return, `permissions/{permission}`. Its id, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/permissions/{permission}`, or its relative name, `permissions/{permission}`. |

### list-permissions

Lists every permission the platform checks, in catalog order, including those no predefined role grants by default, such as the billing account permissions.

```sh
origin iam list-permissions [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### test-iam-permissions

Returns the subset of `--permission` the caller holds on an organization or a project, or on one resource in it. A permission held on the organization counts for each of its projects; one held on a project counts only there. A role binding limited to a list of resources counts only for the resources it lists, never for the organization or the project itself, so asking about the project answers for each of its resources only as far as bindings on the whole project go: name the resource in `--full-resource-name` to have it answered as a call on that resource is. A permission the catalog doesn't name is never held.

```sh
origin iam test-iam-permissions [OPTIONS] --resource <RESOURCE> --permission <PERMISSION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | yes | The organization, `organizations/{organization}`, or the project, `projects/{project}`, to test the permissions on. |
| `--permission <PERMISSION>` | yes | The permissions to test, by their keys, such as `pvs.volume.create`; at most 100. Repeat for more. |
| `--full-resource-name <FULL_RESOURCE_NAME>` | no | The full name of one resource in `--resource` to test the permissions on instead, such as `//secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`: the answer is what a call on that resource is allowed, counting the role bindings that list it as well as those on its organization or project. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` when it isn't a full name, isn't in `--resource` (in the organization, or in the project), or names a kind of resource a role binding can't list: only the bindings on its organization or project apply to such a resource, so testing on the project answers for it. The resource need not exist. Empty to test on `--resource` itself. |

### get-role

Returns a role.

```sh
origin iam get-role [OPTIONS] --role <ROLE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--role <ROLE>` | yes | The role to return, `roles/{role}`. Its id, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/roles/{role}`, or its relative name, `roles/{role}`. |

### list-roles

Lists every predefined role, in catalog order.

```sh
origin iam list-roles [OPTIONS]
```

This command takes no options of its own.

### get-role-binding

Returns a role binding. Needs `iam.member.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-role-binding [OPTIONS] --role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--role-binding` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>` | yes | The binding to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`. |

### list-role-bindings

Lists an organization's role bindings, active and pending, oldest first, optionally only a member's, a project's or a service account's, or only those that apply to one resource. Needs `iam.member.list` on the organization. With the parent `organizations/-` it lists the caller's own active bindings in every organization and needs no permission; `--member` must be empty there.

```sh
origin iam list-role-bindings [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--member <MEMBER>` | no | Only the bindings of this member, by its full name, as a binding's `--member` names it, or a pending binding's `user:{email}`, matched without regard to case. Every member's when empty. |
| `--project <NAME>` | no | Only the bindings limited to this project, by its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`. Every binding, organization-wide or not, when empty. Its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most bindings to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--service-account <NAME>` | no | Only the bindings limited to this service account, by its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Every binding, whatever its scope, when empty. Can't be set together with `--project`: no binding is limited to both. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | no | Only the active bindings that apply to this resource, by its full name, such as `//secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`: those that list it in `resources`, and those with `resources` empty on the organization or on the resource's project, which cover it as a whole. A binding on a service account applies to no resource here, and a pending binding to none until it is active. Every binding when empty. Combines with the other filters. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` when it isn't a full name or names a kind of resource a binding can't list: only the bindings on its organization or project apply to such a resource, which the `--project` filter, or none, lists. |

### create-role-binding

Grants a role to a member. Needs `iam.role.assign` on the organization, for a project binding as well, and every permission of the role at the binding's scope: a permission held on the organization counts for any scope, one held on a project only for that project. A binding with `--resource` needs every permission of the role on each resource it lists: a permission held on the resource's scope counts, and so does one held through a binding that lists the resource. Refused with `NOT_FOUND` when `--member` names a user without an enabled account or a service account of another organization, and when `--service-account` names an account the organization doesn't have. Refused with `CONFLICT` when the member already holds the role at that scope with the same `--resource`, and, for now, also with other `--resource`: a member holds a role at one scope in one binding. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST`, naming the entry, when an entry of `--resource` isn't a full name, is a resource of a kind that can't be listed, is outside the binding's organization or project, or is listed twice; when `--resource` has more than 100 entries, is set together with `--service-account`, or lists a kind of resource none of the role's permissions applies to. Refused with `BAD_REQUEST` when the member is a deleted service account, names no service agent the platform has, or is a service agent and the role isn't one its service needs; when both `--project` and `--service-account` are set; when `--service-account` names a deleted account; and when the role has a permission that doesn't act on one service account, which only `roles/iam.service-account-token-creator` has none of. With `--member` set to `user:{email}`, the account that verified the address is bound, as above. If no enabled account has verified it, the binding is created `PENDING`, organization-wide, and an invitation email is sent to the address. That also needs `iam.member.create` on the organization, and is refused with `BAD_REQUEST` when `--project`, `--service-account` or `--resource` is set and with `CONFLICT` when the address already holds a pending binding of the role in the organization. An address more than one account has verified is refused with `CONFLICT`. Repeated under its `--request-id`, the call answers with the binding it created, pending or since activated.

```sh
origin iam create-role-binding [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --member <MEMBER> --role <NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--member <MEMBER>` | yes | The full name of who holds the role: a user, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, one of the organization's service accounts, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or a platform service agent, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/serviceAgents/{service_agent}`. A pending binding's member is `user:{email}`, the address it was granted to, as typed, until it becomes active. On create, `user:{email}` names a user by email address: see CreateRoleBinding. |
| `--role <NAME>` | yes | The full name of the role granted, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/roles/{role}`. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/roles/{role}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--project <NAME>` | no | The full name of the project the binding is limited to, one of the organization's: `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`. Empty for a binding on the whole organization, which covers every project in it, and for a binding on one service account. Its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--service-account <NAME>` | no | The full name of the service account the binding is limited to, one of the organization's active accounts: `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Such a binding grants its role on that account alone, and nothing on the organization or its projects. Only a role whose every permission acts on one service account can be bound so: `roles/iam.service-account-token-creator`, which lets the member get an access token for that account and no other. Empty for a binding on the whole organization or a project; never set together with `--project`. The binding is removed when the account is deleted. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | no | The full names of the resources the binding is limited to within its organization or project, such as `//secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`, in name order; at most 100. The binding grants its role on these resources alone, and nothing on the rest of its scope or on the organization or the project itself. Empty for a binding on its whole scope. Each entry must be a resource of the binding's organization, in the binding's project if `--project` is set, of a kind that can be listed. Never set together with `--service-account`, nor on a pending binding. A resource deleted after the binding was created stays listed, and the binding covers a resource created later under the same name. The one field UpdateRoleBinding changes. Repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day returns the binding the first request created, as it is now, instead of being refused as a conflict. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-role-binding

Removes a role binding. Needs `iam.role.revoke` on the organization and every permission of the role at the binding's scope, as CreateRoleBinding does. Refused with `CONFLICT`, removing nothing, when it is the organization's last organization-wide binding of `roles/owner`: bind another owner first. Deleting a pending binding withdraws the invitation: signing up with its address afterwards grants nothing.

```sh
origin iam delete-role-binding [OPTIONS] --role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--role-binding` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>` | yes | The binding to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day succeeds as the first did, instead of answering `NOT_FOUND`. One is generated when not given. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### update-role-binding

Replaces the list of resources a binding is limited to, and answers with the binding as it is now. Only the list can change: no other field of a binding can. Give every resource of the new list with `--resource`, or `--no-resources` for an empty list, which widens the binding to its whole scope. The new list replaces the old one at once: the member keeps the role on every entry in both throughout, gains it on the entries added and loses it on those removed. The new list is checked as on `create-role-binding`, and refused with `BAD_REQUEST` for the same entries.

Needs `iam.role.assign` on the organization, and every permission of the role on each resource of the new list and of the old one, as `create-role-binding` and `delete-role-binding` need: a permission held on the binding's scope counts, and so does one held through a binding that lists the resource; for a binding on its whole scope, only one held on that scope counts. Refused with `NOT_FOUND` when the organization has no such binding, and with `BAD_REQUEST` for a pending binding, which is on the whole organization until it is active. Recorded in the audit log, naming the entries added and removed, unless the list stayed the same. Repeated under its `--request-id`, the call answers with the binding as it is now and changes nothing.

```sh
origin iam update-role-binding [OPTIONS] --role-binding <ROLE_BINDING> <--resource <RESOURCE>|--no-resources>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--role-binding` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--role-binding <ROLE_BINDING>` | yes | The role binding to change. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/roleBindings/{role_binding}`. |
| `--resource <RESOURCE>` | one of `--resource`, `--no-resources` | The full names of the resources the binding is limited to within its organization or project, such as `//secretmanager.origincloudapis.eu/projects/{project}/regions/{region}/secrets/{secret}`, in name order; at most 100. The binding grants its role on these resources alone, and nothing on the rest of its scope or on the organization or the project itself. Empty for a binding on its whole scope. Each entry must be a resource of the binding's organization, in the binding's project if `project` is set, of a kind that can be listed. Never set together with `serviceAccount`, nor on a pending binding. A resource deleted after the binding was created stays listed, and the binding covers a resource created later under the same name. The one field UpdateRoleBinding changes. Repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-resources` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-resources` | one of `--resource`, `--no-resources` | Remove all of its resources. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day answers with the binding as it is now, instead of changing it again. One is generated when not given. |

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account to return. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |

### list-service-accounts

Lists an organization's service accounts, oldest first. Deleted ones are listed only when `--show-deleted` is set. Needs `iam.service_account.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-service-accounts [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most service accounts to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--show-deleted <true|false>` | no | Whether deleted service accounts are listed too. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |

### create-service-account

Creates a service account. It has no credential yet: give a `WORKLOAD` one a federated credential, an `EXTERNAL` one a key. Needs `iam.service_account.create` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam create-service-account [OPTIONS] --organization <ORGANIZATION> --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | yes | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. |
| `--display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>` | yes | A name of your own, shown in the console; at most 100 characters. |
| `--type <TYPE>` | no | How the service account authenticates; `EXTERNAL` when the create leaves it unset. Possible values: `EXTERNAL`, `WORKLOAD`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day creates nothing and returns the service account the first request created. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT`. One is generated when not given. |

### delete-service-account

Deletes a service account for good: its credential is refused from then on, an access token it already holds is refused on its next request, and every role binding it holds, in any organization, is removed. It stays readable as `DELETED`. Deleting a deleted service account succeeds. Needs `iam.service_account.revoke` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam delete-service-account [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-service-account-key

Returns a service account key's public metadata, deleted or not; never its private key. Needs `iam.service_account_key.get` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam get-service-account-key [OPTIONS] --key <KEY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` or `--key` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Needed unless `--key` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--key <KEY>` | yes | The key to return. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/keys/{key}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/keys/{key}`. |

### list-service-account-keys

Lists a service account's keys, oldest first, by their public metadata; never a private key. Deleted ones are listed only when `--show-deleted` is set. Needs `iam.service_account_key.list` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam list-service-account-keys [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most keys to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--show-deleted <true|false>` | no | Whether deleted keys are listed too. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |

### create-service-account-key

Creates an `ES256` key for an active `EXTERNAL` service account and returns its private key in `credentialsFile`, in this response only: store it now. Whoever holds the file acts as the service account, so creating a key needs `iam.service_account_key.create` and `iam.service_account.act_as` on the organization. A service account has at most 10 keys that aren't deleted; an 11th is refused with `CONFLICT`. A `WORKLOAD` service account never has a key: it is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

```sh
origin iam create-service-account-key [OPTIONS] --service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT> --credentials-file <CREDENTIALS_FILE>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | yes | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID. A repeat of the request with the same `--request-id` within a day creates nothing and is refused with `CONFLICT`: the private key went to the first request only. The error's `ErrorInfo` metadata names the key under `serviceAccountKey`; delete it and create a new one. The same `--request-id` with a different request is refused with `CONFLICT` without that metadata. One is generated when not given. |
| `--credentials-file <CREDENTIALS_FILE>` | yes | Where to write the key's credentials file, which holds its private key: the API returns it this once, and the platform keeps no copy. It is created readable by you alone; an existing file is refused unless `--overwrite` is given. Point `ORIGINCLOUD_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, or the profile's `credentials-file`, at it to call the API as the service account. |
| `--overwrite` | no | Replace the file `--credentials-file` names when it exists, once the response is in. |

### delete-service-account-key

Deletes a service account key: no assertion signed with it is exchanged from then on. It stays readable as `DELETED`. Deleting a deleted one succeeds. Needs `iam.service_account_key.delete` on the organization.

```sh
origin iam delete-service-account-key [OPTIONS] --key <KEY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--organization <ORGANIZATION>` | no | The organization. Its id, or its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}`. Needed unless `--service-account` or `--key` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--service-account <SERVICE_ACCOUNT>` | no | The service account: its id, completed with `--organization`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Needed unless `--key` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--key <KEY>` | yes | The key to delete. Its id, completed with `--organization` and `--service-account`, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/keys/{key}`, or its relative name, `organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}/keys/{key}`. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-user

Returns the caller's own profile. Any other user is `NOT_FOUND`; a service account caller is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`, having no profile.

```sh
origin iam get-user [OPTIONS] --user <USER>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--user <USER>` | yes | The user to return: `users/me`, or the caller's own `users/{user}`. Its id, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, or its relative name, `users/{user}`. |

### lookup-user

Looks up the user whose account has verified an email address, and answers them with their `name` and their full name, `member`, which is how a role binding names them. Needs `iam.role.assign` on `--organization`, the permission a binding of the user needs anyway. Refused with `NOT_FOUND` when no enabled account has verified the address, and with `CONFLICT` when more than one has. The answer leaves `givenName` and `familyName` empty: only the user reads those.

```sh
origin iam lookup-user [OPTIONS] --email <EMAIL> --organization <NAME>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--email <EMAIL>` | yes | The email address the user's account has verified, matched exactly, case aside. |
| `--organization <NAME>` | yes | The full name of the organization the caller looks the user up for, where it needs `iam.role.assign`: `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`. Its full name, `//resourcemanager.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}`; not a relative name or an id. |

### activate-pending-role-bindings

Activates the role bindings pending for the caller's email address, once the caller's account has verified it, and returns the caller's profile, as GetUser does. Each binding becomes active under its own name with the caller as its member, while whoever created it still holds every permission of its role in the organization; otherwise it is dropped. An address not yet verified activates nothing. Calling it again activates only what has been granted to the address since. A service account caller is refused with `BAD_REQUEST`; any user but the caller is `NOT_FOUND`.

```sh
origin iam activate-pending-role-bindings [OPTIONS] --user <USER>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--user <USER>` | yes | The user whose pending role bindings to activate: `users/me`, or the caller's own `users/{user}`. Its id, or its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/users/{user}`, or its relative name, `users/{user}`. |

## origin sts

The security token service: it turns a token from an identity provider outside Origin Cloud, such as a CI job's OIDC token, into the access token of a `WORKLOAD` service account that trusts it through a federated credential. It authenticates no caller: the token is the proof.

Every `origin sts` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host, `https://sts.origincloudapis.eu`, the same in every region. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_STS_ENDPOINT`. |

### assume-service-account

Assumes a `WORKLOAD` service account with an OIDC token. Exactly one federated credential, of the named service account or of any, must trust the token: its issuer and audience, and every one of its conditions. The token is verified with its issuer's published keys (RS256), and a pull request's job is admitted only by a credential that names its `event_name`. Refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` when the token isn't trusted, without saying why, with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` when it asks for an audience no token is issued for, and with `UNAVAILABLE` when its issuer or the trust can't be read now.

```sh
origin sts assume-service-account [OPTIONS] --oidc-token-file <PATH>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--oidc-token-file <PATH>` | yes | The OIDC token, a JWT its issuer signed, such as a CI job's. Read from the file at the path, or from standard input with `-`, without its final newline. |
| `--service-account <NAME>` | no | The full name of the service account to assume, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`. Only its federated credentials are considered. Without it, any service account's credential that trusts the token is. Its full name, `//iam.origincloudapis.eu/organizations/{organization}/serviceAccounts/{service_account}`; not a relative name or an id. |
| `--lifetime <DURATION>` | no | How long the access token lives: from 60 seconds to 1 hour, 15 minutes when unset. Such as `30s` or `1m`. |
| `--audience <AUDIENCE>` | no | Who the access token is for: `origincloud:api`, the platform's APIs, when unset, or `https://mcp.origincloudapis.eu`, the hosted MCP server. A token for the hosted MCP server isn't accepted by the APIs. Any other audience is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, before the token is checked. |
